newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends weaker as technicals weaken.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends weaker as technicals weaken.

text.p: COMEX copper settled weaker as the market fell on further technical selling after failing to build on any upside gains and break through key chart levels, traders said.
"I think it's getting a little oversold," analyst James Steel of Refco said. "But I would sell any rally over 108.00 to 110.0 cents in the May contract."
May COMEX settled 1.10 cents weaker at 105.15 cents per pound, traded 106.80 to 104.50 cents. Spot April went out 1.60 cents lower at 106.20 cents. Volume was estimated at 9,000 lots.
COMEX stocks rose 141 short tons to 45,608 short tons on Wednesday.

News from Escondida that output would not be hurt if a strike by a small group of workers went ahead Friday, dampened any bullish effect the potential strike may have and prompted some liquidation, traders said.
Commerce Department reported a slightly mixed view on key copper consuming and producing sectors in the U.S.
Housing starts in March fell 6.4 percent to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 1.43 million after a revised 10.7 percent jump in February.
But starts in the first quarter were still ahead of the total for the final quarter of last year.
Manufacturing output rose by a stronger than expected 0.9 percent in March following a revised 0.6 percent February pickup.

Traders said copper prices appeared to shrug off the regular drawdowns in LME stocks, which dipped 1,100 tonnes to 154,675 tonnes on Wednesday, potential labor conflicts at Phelps Dodge's Chino mine and Escondida, and the shutdown later this month of Kennecott's smelter in Utah.
